name: Qajar lithographed book
summary: A book printed from stone. A scribe wrote each page in nastaliq with greasy ink, and the press copied the page as it was. The book looks like a manuscript, with a frame of ruled lines and small painted pictures.

philosophy.core_thesis: A printed book can keep the hand of the scribe and the page of the manuscript, and still be cheap to copy.
design_principles: Write the page by hand in nastaliq on transfer paper; do not set type.
Draw each page inside a frame of ruled lines, with the text in two columns or at a slant.
Keep the manuscript layout: a decorated head piece, a title cartouche and a colophon.
Draw the pictures with a pen in the same ink, with fine line and no tone.
Print in one black ink; add red or a colour wash by hand, after printing.
Print on laid paper with a clear chain line.
Accept a soft edge on the line where the grease spread on the stone.
anti_patterns: Metal type in a regular Latin face
Colour printed in register from many stones

process.matrix: A limestone slab. The scribe writes on transfer paper in lithographic ink, and the paper is pressed on the stone.
process.press: A hand lithographic press with a scraper bar.
process.image_making: A scribe writes the text in nastaliq. A painter draws the pictures with a pen on the same transfer paper.
process.edition: Hundreds to a few thousand copies; the stone is wiped and used again.

inks.strategy: One black lithographic ink for text, frames and pictures. The owner may add red and colour by hand.

colours.name: Hand-tint red
colours.role: a later hand colour on titles and borders

screening.rule: Draw all form as a pen line; make a tone only with the density of the line and with a hand wash after printing.

registration.rule: One stone makes the page, so the register is not a problem; a colour added by hand can sit 1 mm off the line.

substrate.stock: An imported or hand-made laid paper, off-white, with a visible chain line.

surface.impression: A very light bite: the stone prints flat, with no plate mark.
surface.sheen: Matt black with a small grey bloom where the stone was over-wet.
surface.texture: A fine stone grain in the thick strokes and a soft edge on the pen line.

marks: soft grease spread on the line
foxing and chain lines in the paper

evidence.title: Shahnama, a complete lithographed book, dated 1901
evidence.maker: Muhammad Hussein (scribe); Hussain Ali and Muhammad Kazim (pictures)
evidence.credit: Plakasauctions.com via Wikimedia Commons. 1901 is in the reign of Muzaffar al-Din Shah.

lineage.root: The page copies the Persian manuscript book. The data has no earlier print style of this kind; the stone press came from Europe, and Iran used it to print the manuscript hand.

emotion.target_response: Respect for a learned book: the viewer sees a quiet, dense page made by a trained hand.

avoid_when: The brief asks for a loud, modern or photographic image.
The text must be in a Latin face.

modifiers.how: Add 4–6 colour stones, a gold border and a gloss finish.
Replace the hand script with a book face in black and red, on laid paper with wide margins.

sources.title: Persian lithography and Qajar books (Commons file page, 1901 Shahnama)
